chunks: And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a pledge (collateral) taken is [permissible]; and if one trusts the other, then let him who is trusted deliver the thing entrusted, and have fear of God, his Lord. And do not suppress the testimony, and he who conceals it is sinful of heart; and God is aware of all you do.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for securing a loan when traveling and no scribe is available?
ai.summary: While verse 282 establishes the primary protocol for debt documentation, this continuation addresses the practical contingency of travel when a scribe is absent, allowing for tangible collateral (rihan) as a substitute for written records. Shia exegetes highlight the transition from procedural formalism to ethical integrity, emphasizing that the trustee's piety (taqwa) and the preservation of testimony (shahada) are paramount even in the absence of written contracts. This underscores the broader Islamic legal principle that the spirit of trustworthiness supersedes mere technical compliance in financial dealings.
